subject: Re: Harmon Health - request/response scrubbing and residency clarifications
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Harmon Health - post-call: header & body scrubbing + residency clarifications

Hi Anika / Liam / security team —

Thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard (short):
- Harmon needs request/response logging for incident investigation but must ensure PHI/PII is never retained in raw logs.
- Primary concerns: headers (trace IDs, patient identifiers passed in headers), response bodies that may contain free-text notes, and storage residency (US-only) + retention windows.
- You prefer pseudonymization (hashing) for trace IDs rather than full removal, but need confirmation from your security team on re-identification risk and retention policy.

Redwood proposal (actionable):
1) Default Apache-style request/response log pipeline with two scrubbing layers: header-level suppression + token-level body redaction.
2) Trace IDs: implement HMAC-hashing with a per-customer salt stored in your KMS. Hash values are one-way by default; we can provide deterministic hashing for cross-request linking if you allow a reversible escrow under strict controls.
3) Sampling and retention: keep full request IDs for 7 days in hot store, hashed IDs + metadata for 90 days in encrypted cold storage (US-only region).
4) Deliverables for your security review: a short spec (attached), samples showing before/after scrubbing (attached), and a short demo of the scrub pipeline.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Harmon security (Anika / Liam): confirm whether deterministic hashing is acceptable (yes/no by Wed 5/24).
- Redwood (Karthik / Monica): produce a one-page threat model for the hashing option and a scrub demo (ETA Mon 5/27).
- Vanessa: schedule a 30-min follow-up demo with engineering + security (proposed Thu 5/30).

Attachments: redaction-spec-v1.pdf (high-level flow), sample-logs-scrubbed.csv (sanitized examples).

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Subject: Re: Harmon Health - post-call: header & body scrubbing + residency clarifications

Thanks Vanessa — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side before we get the threat model: 

1) Deterministic hashing: our SREs use trace linking for debugging patient flows. We prefer deterministic hashing so we can join traces, but only if the salt cannot be retrieved by ops people. Can you outline mechanisms for a KMS-backed salt where only a small number of keys are usable for the hashing operation (no export)?

2) Response body scrubbing: do you support rule-based redaction (regex + named entity lists) and an ML fallback for free-text clinical notes? We need high recall on patient identifiers; false positives are OK as long as we log redaction hits for audit.

3) Residency: US-only is a hard requirement for the logs store. Can you provide an attestation for where the cold backups are stored (cloud provider + region)?

We can confirm deterministic hashing acceptance by Wed if the KMS constraint is feasible. Also, we want to see the sample logs and the demo before the security review.

-Anika
Head of Security, Harmon Health
security@harmonhealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Harmon Health - post-call: header & body scrubbing + residency clarifications

Anika — quick technical notes and feasibility points from infra/serving runtime: 

- KMS-backed deterministic hashing: feasible. Implementation pattern we recommend: HMAC-SHA256 with a non-exportable key in your KMS. Redwood will call a KMS Sign API to generate the HMAC; the key never leaves KMS and ops cannot retrieve the raw key material. We will store only the HMAC outputs (hex) in logs.

- ML + rule-based scrubbing: we support a two-pass pipeline. Pass 1: deterministic rules (regex + whitelist/blacklist) executed at edge; Pass 2: a lightweight ML model runs in the scrub service to catch edge cases in free text. Every redaction emits a redaction-event record (type, confidence, field, rule-id) into an audit topic for your SOC to review.

- Residency and backups: Redwood Dedicated/Private offers US-only buckets in our Gov-like tenancy. For Hosted customers we can pin logs to a US region and configure cross-region backups to be disabled. We will provide a signed attestation doc listing provider + region (example: AWS us-west-2 for hot, us-west-2 Glacier for cold).

Attachments: redaction-spec-v1.pdf (the same doc Vanessa attached), sample-logs-scrubbed.csv (sanitized)

Open items we will address in the follow-up demo:
- Demo: show deterministic-hash linking without key export (Karthik).
- Threat model: short write-up on re-identification risk and operational controls (Monica).
- Redaction audit trace: sample audit stream and retention model (Rishi).

I'll prepare the demo environment and share a calendar link for Thu 5/30 11:00am PT.

If Harmon is comfortable after the demo, we can move to a short pilot: 2 weeks of scrubbed logs ingestion from a single stage environment and a joint security review. Post-pilot we can scope per-environment retention SLAs in the contract (RDW-5821).

I'll also share the DocuSign NDA/PO templates you asked about in a separate thread — want to keep the security convo focused.
